newsitem.title: POLAND: POLIFARB CN, POLIFARB W TO MERGE.
newsitem.headline: POLIFARB CN, POLIFARB W TO MERGE.

text.p: Poland's two listed paintmakers, Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw, said in separate statements on Thursday that they had agreed to merge their operations.
"On December 17 the company signed an agreement with Polifarb Cieszyn SA on the conditions of a planned merger of the two companies," Polifarb Wroclaw said in its statement.

It said that the agreement between the companies' managements envisioned a full merger of the two firms with Polifarb Cieszyn taking over all the assets of its Wroclaw-based namesake in return for a new share issue for Wroclaw's shareholders.
Polifarb Wroclaw shareholders would receive one Polifarb Cieszyn share for each Wroclaw share.
The statement said the new company's headquarters would be based in Wroclaw, southwestern Poland.
It also said the agreement needed shareholder approval of both companies.

"The decision...requires the approval of shareholders of both companies...so the management boards are not allowed to take any legally binding steps, and there is by no means any obligation for a merger," the statement said.
It also said the companies by the end of this year would ask the anti-monopoly office to clear the planned merger.
No company officials were immediately available for comment.

Jacek Dzierwa, an equity analyst at Salomon Bros in London, said the merger plan would likely boost both companies' market standings and was likely a response to increasing competition from foreign producers such as Dutch Akzo-Nobel .
"I regard this as a very positive move, the first such in Warsaw bourse history," Dzierwa told Reuters.
He said the price of both stocks would likely soar in the next few sessions.
Polifarb Cieszyn had sales of 289.4 million zlotys in this year's first 11 months. Polifarb Wroclaw had 196 million in sales over the same period. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
